VBO:0201371.summary: Alert and keen to hunt, the Treeing Cur finds game through sight, hearing and scent. It may give voice or stay quiet while tracking, with a distinct change when quarry reaches a tree. Rural American breeders selected these versatile dogs for performance, combining hunting with guarding and livestock work.
VBO:0201371.shortDescription: An alert tree dog using sight, hearing and scent, with voice on the trail varying between individuals.

VBO:0201372.summary: Highly alert, the Treeing Feist hunts through both sight and scent and tends to remain almost silent while following a trail. Generations of performance breeding in the rural American South shaped its small-game work. Squirrel hunting remains central, with raccoon, opossum, rabbits and flushing game birds also among its uses.
VBO:0201372.shortDescription: An alert, usually quiet tracker using sight and scent, with squirrel hunting central to its working history.

VBO:0201409.summary: Independent and self-reliant, the Welsh Hound is a hunter shaped by rugged, rocky country. It follows low scent and uses a talkative voice that carries across windy Welsh hills. Organized hunts have maintained packs of these native hounds through a long regional hunting tradition.
VBO:0201409.shortDescription: An independent Welsh pack hound, shaped by rocky hills and known for a carrying, talkative voice.

VBO:0201302.summary: A fast, keen hunter, the Stephens’ Cur often carries its head high while following a trail and has a strong instinct to mark quarry in trees. Hugh Stephens’s Kentucky family developed this distinct line from Mountain Cur stock. Its main work is hunting squirrel and raccoon, with packs also used for larger game.
VBO:0201302.shortDescription: A keen tree dog from Kentucky, known for following trails with its head high and hunting squirrel and raccoon.

sources.title: Stephens’ Cur: Official UKC Breed Standard
